rows.semantic: promisor metadata alone (extensions.partialClone, remote.*.promisor, partialclonefilter, paired .promisor+.pack) is not a refusal: a complete promisor-marked repository keeps the verdict of its full-clone twin

failed_row_detail.stderr_tail: could-not-evaluate: 1234567890abcdef1234567890abcdef12345678: unknown: absence is uncertain (blanket refusal)

rows.semantic: the unknown rule covers a locally unresolved citation that names unavailable referenced content; it must not cover every absent citation, or the historical errata-marked clone (absent hash corrected by errata) would stop being an ordinary failed finding. The mutant refuses every absent (or unknown) citation, before the errata ledger is consulted.

objects the audit actually reads must be available: a missing required commit/tree/blob/report object is could-not-evaluate (exit 2), never a clean or failed verdict. This mutant removes the store's missing-object computation (the completeness element); PM04 removes the decision that uses it. Both attack the same verdict surface, so the grid kills them alike: one of them surviving is not evidence about the other.
a locally unresolved citation that names unavailable referenced local content is could-not-evaluate rather than proved absent; the mutant accepts it as absent and reports an ordinary failed finding
a citation missing in one audited repository but present in the other audited repository is resolvable; the mutant consults the first repository only
a failing read of the object the audit needs is could-not-evaluate; the mutant swallows the failure and guesses a value, turning an unavailable object into a verdict

the missing-object traversal is rooted at the pinned lane/fleet roots the audit reads; the mutant roots it at --all, so an unrelated missing historical object refuses an otherwise complete repository. Note: the candidate's own traversal already starts from every commit the local object database holds, so this mutant can be observationally identical there; a survivor is evidence about the candidate's traversal scope, not about the grid.

rows.reason: --no-lazy-fetch present before=True after=True; not executed: a fixture that could reach a transport is forbidden in this wave
rows.semantic: every git call carries --no-lazy-fetch, so a missing promisor object can never be fetched through the promisor remote (transport, repository programs, signatures); removing the flag reopens that channel
the bare full-hash lookup stays unpeeled: a citation of a locally present blob resolves as found; peeling it to ^{commit} turns a present blob into a missing object

when a citation is unresolved, a missing tree or commit may conceal the dependency names, so the citation is unevaluable (exit 2); the mutant ignores that opaque non-leaf hole and reports an ordinary failed finding. A known-present blob that merely fails commit peeling keeps its wrong-type finding either way.

no missing-object state may be an unconditional audit precondition: an unrelated blob hole next to a fabricated citation keeps the ordinary failed finding, and an unused tree hole next to fully resolved citations keeps the clean verdict; the mutant refuses on any hole
